lines.text: CHURCH OF GOD
SUNDAY SCHOOL QUARTERLY
"EXCEPT" OR
ESSENTIALS FOR SALVATION
"EXCEPT" OR ESSENTIALS FOR SALVATION
CONTENTS
Except Ye Believe on Jesus Christ. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . 8
Except Shedding of Blood Is No Remission . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . 13
Except Ye Become as Little Children . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . 21
Except Your Righteousness Exceed. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . 27
NOTE TO THE TEACHERS
This booklet is intended to be a help in preparing Sunday school
lessons. The title, subject, and topics are only the menu. It is your
responsibility to prepare the meal.
The proper ingredients are the salty inspirations of the Holy Spirit,
seasoned with His grace. Bake the ingredients at a hot temperature in
the oven of prayer. The time-tested recipe for preparing a nutritious
meal is found in 2 Timothy 2:15, "Study to shew thyself approved
unto God, a workman that needeth not to be ashamed, rightly dividing
the word of truth."
LESSON 1
EXCEPT A MAN BE BORN AGAIN
Scripture Texts: Jeremiah 13:23; John 1:1-13, 3:3; 2 Corinthians 5:17;
In this quarterly, we will look at essentials of salvation—requirements
without which there is no salvation. Each of these, many of which may be
called "exceptions," is a supernatural work of God in the heart. Our part
is to obey Him.
Skilled workmen know they must follow certain procedures exactly or
fail. Trained workmen and precision tools are required for many jobs. Na-
tural laws are sought and followed. Spiritual laws are just as exact.
MEMORY VERSE: Jesus answered and said unto him, Verily, verily, I say
unto thee, Except a man be born again, he cannot see the kingdom of God.
—John 3:3
The Necessity of Rebirth
Have we not heard, "It does not matter where we worship, just so one
is sincere" or "We are all going to the same place; we are all brothers" or
"Everyone has a right to his belief; one is as good as another"? Are these
statements true? There is only ONE way to spiritual life—the RIGHT way.
It is given in the Bible. Wrong directions and ignorant guidance have re-
sulted in the loss of many a soul. To follow opinions of men rather than
God's essentials of truth is tragic.
Since "all have sinned" (Romans 3:23), therefore all come under the
truth of the statement found in Jeremiah 13:23. We cannot do good. By
man's standards, there seem to be unsaved people doing good all around
us. How about God's standard? There is none good but God, as it is written
in Luke 18:19. God counts nothing as good except that which proceeds
from Him.
A natural, unsaved man is a dead soul. A reborn man is alive, with God
living within him. We cannot rid ourselves of sin because it is a part of us
as much as spots are a part of the leopard. The only way to be rid of the
spots of sin is to have them removed by the miraculous work of God. This
takes place through the new birth, or the rebirth that makes us new per-
sons, as we read in John 3:3. By being born again, we enter the Kingdom
of God—there is no other way. This is a divine change.
The Way of Rebirth
John 14:6 plainly tells us rebirth, spiritual birth, comes through one
Person and one only—Jesus Christ. He gave His life on the Cross, which
enabled Him to give mankind a new life, a new birth. He died so that we
may live. We become sons of God, not by natural birth, but by spiritual
birth into God's family. To do this, we must receive Christ by repenting
and believing the Gospel, as we read in Mark 1:15. Repentance is turning
from sin in heartfelt sorrow. The Gospel tells us to believe on Christ's
name. This includes believing His identity as God, trusting and believing
that He (through the sacrifice of His life) can and will save us from sin.
The Result of Rebirth
2 Corinthians 5:17 If any man be in Christ ... he is born again, he is
a new creature. He has a new life—at first as a babe in Christ, then grow-
ing to a mature Christian. Many have joined a church but have never been
born from above. Often they live good lives by worldly standards, but they
have not been taught the truth of the Scriptures, which teaches that they
must become new creatures, not just good people. Whose plan is "church
joining"? How does it compare with the new birth? Is "church joining"
Biblical?
1 John 3:9 Whosoever is born of God doth not commit sin. Some
teach that there are two types of sinners—"saved sinners" and "unsaved
sinners." In 1 John 3:10, we find God counts all sinners as children of
the devil. Sin is a nature separated from God, a disposition to disobey
God. The new birth puts in us the nature of God, godliness, and obedience
to Him.
Begun here, the godly life is to go on after death. To be born of God
starts us toward everlasting life in Heaven. The new birth gives LIFE,
HOLINESS (which is sinlessness and godliness), and FUTURE HOPE.
There can be no future hope without a new life and holiness.
JUST A THOUGHT
Almost anything can be bought at a reduced price
except lasting satisfaction.
LESSON 2
EXCEPT YE REPENT
Scripture Texts: Psalm 38:3-4; Matthew 5:23-26, 7:13-14; Luke 13:1-2;
2 Corinthians 7:9-11; 1 John 1:9; Proverbs 28:13; Isaiah 55:7; Psalm
Last week, we studied about being born again, the new birth. There are
steps that must be taken to gain this experience of a new birth. Today we
learn about the first steps—repent of and forsake sin.
MEMORY VERSE: I tell you, Nay: but, except ye repent, ye shall all like-
wise perish.
—Luke 13:3
What Is Repentance?
Our first step to salvation is repentance. There is no salvation without
it. It is difficult for the flesh to yield and humble itself down, but it yields
a reward of forgiveness, peace, and joy. Psalm 38:3-4 tells us that sin is
a heavy burden. Nothing can hurt as much as the pain of a guilty con-
science. All understand this, for all have felt it. David was overwhelmed
by his sin and by the displeasure of God. Conviction held him as it holds
men today. Thank God, we can be free. This is possible by confessing,
repenting, forsaking sin, and trusting in the only Savior, Jesus Christ.
Luke 13:1-2 Jesus impressed upon His disciples the need for repen-
tance, which ALL humanity shares. Some of these Galileans appeared to
have more sin than others, but any sin damns the soul. God's verdict is the
same for all—repent or perish. God measures the repentance, not the sin.
Matthew 7:13-14 Enter ... in at the strait gate ... unto life. Both the
strait and the wide gates are before us early in life. We begin life or de-
struction here. Why is it that few ... find life? It is not because God hides
the gate. He has given us the Gospel. It is because repentance is the gate,
and repentance is hard and painful. Repentance is to become tired of the
ways of sin and to be sorry that we have ever sinned against God.
Confession of Sin
1 John 1:9 To have our sins forgiven, they must be confessed. We can-
not name out every sin we have committed. We simply acknowledge our
guilt and humbly ask forgiveness for all our wrongs, and God is faithful
and just to forgive us of all our sins and make us clean from all unrigh-
teousness. To be rid of guilt, confession must be made to those who were
wronged. Before God, the heart must be laid bare and the sin owned.
Proverbs 28:13 He that covereth his sins shall not prosper. He may
feel that he has his sins covered, but God will uncover them for all to see.
The only cover for sins is the blood of Jesus Christ, the only Savior of the
souls of mankind. Psalm 34:18 tells us that a broken heart and a contrite
spirit are a part of repentance.
Forsaking of Sin
2 Corinthians 7:9-11 Godly sorrow has a part in repentance to salva-
tion. Heartfelt sorrow causes you to hate and turn from sin. It breeds care-
fulness. There is a clearing of yourselves. You clean up your conduct,
make restitution, feel indignation at your wrong acts, and have a fear of
God's wrath. You also have a vehement desire to be free of guilt and to
do right in the future, a zeal to make a thorough change, and a desire of
revenge to destroy the works of Satan.
Isaiah 55:7 At the heart of repentance, there is a forsaking, a change
of direction, conduct, living, goals, masters. Without this, confession and
sorrow are fruitless. The change is outward and inward. Beware at this
point of going along on your own efforts, which will end only in failure.
Put your full trust in God to begin the work of salvation and return to
Him each day to continue the work in you. You will then experience His
loving mercy, abundant pardon, peace, and joy. God and His angels re-
joice with us when we find true salvation. True repentance is found only
where there is a complete change of heart toward God.
JUST A THOUGHT
Regret for sin or remorse over sin
is not repentance.
LESSON 3
EXCEPT THE FATHER DRAW YOU
Scripture Texts: John 6:44-45; 1 Corinthians 1:9; Romans 2:4; Acts 2:37-
Jesus died for our sins. God (the Father), the Holy Spirit, and the Word
of God all have a great part in our salvation. Conviction works in the heart
of a sinner. It is important and needful that we feel the convicting and
drawing influence of God. We cannot choose our own time to be saved.
The result of refusing the drawing of God is always of a serious nature.
The right response to the drawing of conviction is to yield to it.
MEMORY VERSE: No man can come to me, except the Father which hath
sent me draw him: and I will raise him up at the last day. —John 6:44
The Father's Part in Salvation
Before we can repent and receive Christ through salvation, we must be
drawn to it by the supernatural touch of the Father. He sends conviction
of sin and a desire for Jesus Christ.
All three Persons of the Godhead work together in bringing this work
of conviction. None of Them can be said to accomplish any work by Him-
self, independently of the Others. Yet, each has certain phases of divine
work in which He leads and the Others support.
John 6:44-45 Jesus invites us to come unto Him. We may think it is all
in our hands, that we can put it off or choose our time and way to come.
Not so. The Father must touch our hearts to draw us. It is a supernatural
work. If we heed His drawing, if we hear and learn of Him, His truth will
draw us toward Jesus to be saved. The greatest privilege and honor that
man can experience in this life is to be spoken to by the Spirit of God and
offered salvation through conviction.
1 Corinthians 1:9 God calls us. We should answer. "He, that being
often reproved hardeneth his neck, shall suddenly be destroyed, and that
without remedy" (Proverbs 29:1). The Holy Spirit is the Agent through
whom the Father draws us. Jesus spoke of Him as "the Holy Ghost, whom
the Father will send in my name" (John 14:26). One of the Spirit's func-
tions is to "reprove [or convict] the world of sin, and of righteousness, and
of judgment" (John 16:8). This is the influence on the heart that we call
conviction.
Workings of Conviction
A man in the grasp of conviction feels his sin and suffers the pain of
guilt. He sees God's righteousness and longs to possess it. He realizes his
life is laid bare to the all-seeing eye of God. These are the strong cords by
which the Father draws us. Romans 2:4 tells us that the goodness of God
leadeth thee to repentance. The hard step of repentance is a good step
because it leads to the entrance of life everlasting. It opens to us the King-
dom of God. The Father sends the persuasions of conviction because He
loves us. We are told in 2 Peter 3:9 that He is "not willing that any should
perish, but that all should come to repentance."
Acts 2:37-39 is a good example of the workings of conviction. Newly
filled with the Holy Spirit, Peter preached, exalting Christ and accusing
the people of His Crucifixion. The Spirit fastened truth in their hearts.
They were pricked in their hearts—conviction seized them. To escape the
results of their guilt, they cried, "What shall we do?" They obeyed Peter's
command to repent and be baptized. They were valid candidates for
baptism when they had repented and were born spiritually. Continued
obedience, joy, and victory followed. The Word of God activated by the
Holy Spirit brought conviction. God's Word still brings conviction when
it is applied with godly love and prayer. Hebrews 4:12 tells us the reason.
Our Response
Acts 3:19 Repent ... that your sins may be blotted out, when the
times of refreshing shall come. God sends these times. These are the
times when it is most easy to heed, yield, and be filled with life. Most can
remember a time of refreshing in a service when God's call was louder,
His drawing was stronger, and His joy was greater. These times come
from the Lord. We do not send them.
When influence, providence, and circumstances so combine as to allow
His call to reach us, we should heed. A time we might set, after neglecting
or refusing His call, might find us too hardened to hear it.
James 4:7-10 When the Father draws us, what is our part? Submit ...
to God and resist the devil. Draw nigh to God. Cleanse your hands
(make right outward sins). Purify your hearts (cast out sinful thoughts
and motives). Be afflicted, and mourn, and weep (sorrow for sin). Hum-
ble yourselves in the sight of the Lord. These are true characteristics of
repentance. The fruit of repentance is forgiveness, cleansing, and life in
Christ. Our response is to obey at the first drawing of the Father.
JUST A THOUGHT
It is what we have in our hearts that makes us thankful,
not what we have on the table.
LESSON 4
EXCEPT YE BELIEVE ON JESUS CHRIST
Hebrews 11:6; 1 John 5:5
The way of life is believing. Repentance, which we have studied in an
earlier lesson, is a NEGATIVE step. It is ridding yourself of sin. It is turn-
ing from and emptying out. Believing is POSITIVE. It is a turning to, an
accepting or receiving the life of Christ Himself. You are not saved, or not
alive in Christ until you have believed on Christ.
MEMORY VERSE: He that believeth on the Son hath everlasting life: and
he that believeth not the Son shall not see life; but the wrath of God abid-
eth on him.
—John 3:36
The Way to Life
Believing on Jesus Christ completes the requirement for receiving
Christ—being saved. This is belief in Christ's deity and power and love.
It is full dependence upon His sacrifice to pay for our sins. What kind of
believing transforms a dead soul into a living one? Not merely accepting
the fact that Christ lived nor the mental belief that He is good and God's
Son. No, it is an opening of the heart to receive. God performs open-heart
surgery on all who are saved. It is felt as much as thought.
John 3:16 Whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have
everlasting life. Does not believing IN make it more positive than believ-
ing ON?
John 5:24 He that heareth my word—listens, receives—is passed
from death unto life. Do we not have to listen to hear? What we listen to
and hear has much to do with what we receive. Not with fleshly ears, but
"with the heart man believeth unto righteousness" (Romans 10:10). In this
he is passed from death unto life. "This is the first resurrection" (Revela-
tion 20:5). Now, we have just begun to live. Anything less than life in
Christ Jesus is merely existing.
Hindrances to Believing
John 5:44-46 One attitude that shuts out belief is seeking honor of
men, of having our values out of perspective. Worldly values are external
and fleeting. The honor God gives is quiet, spiritual, lasting, and precious.
Jesus spoke of the hindrance of unbelief in His Word. Jesus' hearers fol-
lowed Moses in form but disbelieved his inspired writings (the first five
books of the Old Testament). Today belief in the truthfulness and divine
origin of the Bible is a basis for belief in Christ (John 17:17).
Dependence upon your own efforts is another hindrance to belief in
Christ. True belief in Him is dependence upon Him. It is casting yourself
upon His mercy. It is taking His death as payment for your sins. Some
asked Jesus, "What shall we do, that we might work the works of God?"
(John 6:28). They were asking, "What act, great effort, gift, kind deed,
sacrifice, or penance should we do to earn salvation, to produce life?"
God wants none of these. They cannot produce life eternal. The death
of Jesus Christ purchased our salvation. Yield to His work, cast yourself
upon it, believe He saves. Hebrews 4:10 says, "For he that is entered into
his rest, he also hath ceased from his own works, as God did from his."
Necessity of Believing
Acts 8:36-37 The Ethiopian asked Philip for baptism, the symbol and
testimony of the new birth. Philip laid down one condition—If thou be-
lievest with all thine heart. Believing goes before conviction and repen-
tance. The Ethiopian believed that Jesus Christ is the Son of God. Jesus
Himself said this belief is necessary (John 8:24).
Hebrews 11:6 In order to come to God, we must believe that he is. No
atheist is saved. No agnostic is saved. The first believes there is no God.
The other is not sure. The Christian is sure that God lives and that Jesus
Christ is God, being the Father's Son. He believes both God's ability and
His willingness to save, both His power and His love. These truths God
says we must believe.
What prepares us to place faith in Christ so much as believing that the
Bible is God's Word? Does any other authority bear as great weight with
an inquirer as to be shown a Bible statement?
Consider this illustration of believing and depending on God, or of de-
pending on self: A little girl started for Sunday school wearing a new
dress. "Take my hand," said Daddy. "It is icy and very slippery."
"No, I can walk by myself." A few steps and down she went, messing
the pretty dress. Tearfully back to Daddy she turned.
"Now will you take my hand?" he asked.
"No, carry me, Daddy."
Power in Believing
1 John 5:5 In the search for power many miss the greatest power—that
over sin and self (overcometh the world). We get it by believing that Je-
sus is the Son of God. This means letting go of self and casting our
broken hearts at the feet of Jesus, trusting His blood to cleanse from all
sin and give us life. When repentance and faith are complete, the soul is
born again a child of God.
We dedicate ourselves to what we truly believe. The teachings of evo-
lution and modernism rest upon unbelief of God's Word. How can we pro-
tect ourselves and others from their poison? How can we counteract the
slogan, "There are no absolutes"? Truth never changes.
Parent, you have in your hands much of the believing of your children.
The greater influence is in their early years. They must be taught to love,
respect, read, and obey the Bible as the absolute authority. Can you be-
lieve for another? Where does this leave infant baptism?
JUST A THOUGHT
It is not only necessary to have faith in a good cause,
we must also make an investment in it.
LESSON 5
EXCEPT YE FORGIVE OTHERS
Scripture Texts: Matthew 6:12-15; Luke 6:36-37; 17:3-4; Romans 12:19-
20; Ephesians 4:32
Most agree it is right to forgive. Many wish they could. Some do. How
is forgiveness brought about? Forgiveness is conditional. Many people
find it too difficult to forgive others and thus find themselves unable to
obtain forgiveness from God.
MEMORY VERSE: But if ye forgive not men their trespasses, neither will
your Father forgive your trespasses.
—Matthew 6:15
Forgiveness Is Dependent
Since all have sinned, all need forgiveness. When we see our sin
through the Spirit's convincing power and yield to the Father's drawing
and repent, we crave forgiveness. God is ready to give it. Why then are
some not forgiven? Forgiveness is conditional. Jesus said so. God can
forgive only a heart that is willing to forgive.
To be forgiven one must be willing to forsake all sin. A grudge, hatred,
desire for revenge, bitterness—these are sins. An unforgiving heart is
closed. God can put His forgiveness into an open heart only. God's pur-
pose in doing a work in our hearts is to make us like Him. He is loving,
merciful, and forgiving. If He is not allowed to make us like that, He can
do nothing at all. That person remains unforgiven, unsaved, without hope
of Heaven.
Ability to Forgive
Matthew 6:12-15 Jesus is our example. On the Cross He forgave His
murderers. We will not have more to forgive than He. We will have His
help in doing it. Unsaved persons cannot muster a forgiving attitude, but
they must have a willingness to give God opportunity to help them to
forgive.
Luke 17:3 All suffer injuries at times. Sometimes we may rebuke the
offender (point out his offense). If he repent, forgive him. If he does not
repent, forgive him. He cannot receive this forgiveness until he comes and
asks for it. Our watching must be of self rather than of the other fellow.
We are admonished to take heed to yourselves.
Forgiveness does not bring about a bad memory. We may not forget the
act, but we will not remember the wrong. We will not hold a judging and
condemning attitude. We bury it with never a thought of digging it up
again, ever.
Response to Injuries
Romans 12:19-20 gives us good instruction. Vengeance and the love
of God do not dwell in a heart at the same time. A desire to get even, to
pay back a wrong, is sinful. To do kindness to the offender is right and
blesses doubly: (1) it nourishes the love and forgiveness in the offended
one's heart, and (2) it persuades toward repentance in the heart of the of-
fender. The coals of fire on his head mean conviction in his heart. No
vindictive punishment could produce this.
Give place unto wrath—give way or yield before the wrath of an ene-
my rather than to retaliate. Wrath is a work of the flesh that will keep us
from the Kingdom of God (Galatians 5:20-21). We cannot afford to harbor
it. Adam Clarke suggested this means to leave the matter to civil law and
to God to judge and punish. Or "yield a little to a man when he is in a
violent passion, for the sake of peace, until he grows cooler." The very
fact that we have been forgiven creates in us a desire to forgive.
Effects of an Unforgiving Spirit
People who refuse to forgive hold resentment, bitterness, and revenge
against others. In some cases, people hold unforgiveness toward God.
Their lives are void of the joy and peace that only God can supply. They
are misfits in the congregation. They are of no help in God's service. They
are the cause of evil gossip. Their speech and actions are affected by their
unforgiveness. We must never ask ourselves if they deserve forgiveness.
Ephesians 4:32 None of us were deserving of God's forgiveness. God
did not give us justice, He gave us forgiveness. We are to forgive because
we have received forgiveness. We are to forgive because God forgives. He
is our example. His nature is ours if we are His children. "Except" we for-
give our brother, we cannot be forgiven.
JUST A THOUGHT
No matter how long a fellow nurses a grudge,
it will not get better.
LESSON 6
EXCEPT SHEDDING OF BLOOD IS NO REMISSION
Scripture Texts: Leviticus 17:11; Exodus 24:6-8; Matthew 26:27-28;
Ephesians 1:7; Hebrews 9:11-28; 10:12-19; Revelation 12:11
Leviticus 17:11 The life ... is in the blood. God ordained the system
of animal sacrifices as a symbol of the coming Sacrifice of Christ. Even
before Christ came, sin could be atoned for only by the shedding of blood.
Animal sacrifices atoned temporarily until time for the final sacrifice.
This final sacrifice was Christ. His blood was necessary for salvation. Ex-
cept we trust in the blood of Christ, shed for us and in our place, there is
no forgiveness of sin.
MEMORY VERSE: And almost all things are by the law purged with
blood; and without shedding of blood is no remission. —Hebrews 9:22
Covenants Sealed With Blood
Exodus 24:6-8 When God made His covenant of the Law with Israel,
Moses took the blood of sacrifices and sprinkled it on the altar (repre-
senting God's side) and sprinkled it on the people. It bound God to His
promises to bless Israel and be their God. It bound Israel to their promises
to keep His Law.
Matthew 26:27-28 When Jesus was about to sacrifice Himself, He
gave the symbol of His shed blood (grape juice) to His disciples, calling
it my blood of the new testament, or the new covenant. A better covenant
was taking the place of the old. His blood bound Him and His people to-
gether—He to save from sin; they to receive, trust, and obey Him.
The Blood of the Lamb
Why is Jesus called our Passover? Why is He called the Lamb of God?
As God prepared Israel to escape from Egypt, He instructed them to kill
the Passover lamb. The Israelites applied the blood as they were instructed
and were saved from death. They ate the flesh of the lamb and received
strength for their journey. Does Jesus fulfill this type?
Power of the Blood
Ephesians 1:7 Through Christ's blood we have forgiveness of sins.
Our guilt is blotted out. Also, through it we have redemption. That is,
Christ's sacrifice "buys back" from Satan all who repent and trust Him. It
frees those who repent from sin's bondage. God does not forgive and leave
us in sin. He gives us the power to keep from sinning. He also frees us
from sin's final result, which is Hell.
Hebrews 9:11-28 The writer looked back into the religious history of
Israel and saw the blood shed by many sacrifices. This blood of animals
was effective for purifying material articles that were patterns of things
that would follow in the new dispensation. The cleansing power of animal
blood was limited. It was only a type of a greater cleansing to come.
Hebrews 10:12-14 Nothing but blood could purify material patterns.
Animal blood could do that only if applied in divine order, but to cleanse
a soul from sin takes divine blood. Only the blood of Jesus Christ suffices.
This is the teaching of the Bible, and the Bible is the Word of God. One
offering is enough if its quality is perfect for the need. The sacrifice of
Christ is. None other will be made to sanctify us and set us apart to God.
Revelation 12:11 Three means by which the martyrs of the early
church overcame Satan are: (1) the blood of the Lamb—faith in Christ's
shed blood puts within them life in Christ, power, purity, and light—cast-
ing out the corruption, ignorance, and falseness of paganism; (2) their
testimony; and (3) the consecration of their lives even unto the death.
These weapons are available to all God's people when they take complete
faith in the blood of Jesus Christ that was shed on Calvary's Cross.
Jesus died to pay our debt for sin. He died to give us life—His life.
Jesus did a work on the Cross that no other could do, the greatest ever
done in the world. Have you entered into this holiest place that the blood
of Jesus opens to us? If not, as far as you are concerned, Christ died in
vain. Do not let your portion be wasted.
JUST A THOUGHT
The loneliest place in the world is the human heart
when love is absent.
LESSON 7
EXCEPT YE EAT MY FLESH
Scripture Texts: John 6:51-63; Matthew 26:26-28; 1 John 5:12; 2 Peter
1:4; Hebrews 10:16; John 4:14; 1 Corinthians 1:30
The process in physical life is to be born to live and eat to keep living.
In our lesson today, we study the spiritual analogy to this. Be born of the
Spirit (Lesson 1) to live, partake of Christ to nourish that life, and grow
in grace. If a soul brought to life is not fed, it will soon die. Matthew 5:6
teaches us the truth of this. Open your heart wide to Him. Hunger for and
desire Him. Could failure to do this explain the loss of many souls from
the rank of the newly saved?
MEMORY VERSE: Then Jesus said unto them, Verily, verily, I say unto
you, Except ye eat the flesh of the Son of man, and drink his blood, ye have
no life in you.
—John 6:53
Eating Christ's Flesh
John 6:51-58 How does one eat and drink of Christ? The people ques-
tioned Jesus' comparison of Himself to the manna God gave the Israelites.
The very thought of eating Christ's flesh was repulsive to the Jews. The
manna was a type of Jesus, the true bread which came down from heav-
en that nourishes the spiritual life of man. When Jesus said we must eat
His flesh and drink His blood to have life, He spoke of our spiritual life
that is much more important than our physical life. Unless we take Christ
into ourselves, unless we open our hearts wide and take Him in to live
there, we are dead souls.
First Corinthians 10:1-4 tells us that all the people partook of Christ
even back in Moses' day. They were partaking of spiritual meat and spir-
itual drink. First Corinthians 10:16-17 speaks of the blood and body of
Christ.
John 6:51-63 Jesus made it clear that He was speaking figuratively, as
a parable, saying flesh to mean spirit. He pictured the relative value of the
flesh and the spirit. What a vast difference. Do we value them as He does?
In Galatians 6:8, we find the Spirit to be life and the flesh to be death. The
Bible is God's written Word. It is a living Book because it leads us to
Christ who is life. Jesus is the living Word. To eat and drink of Christ, we
must begin by reading, but the Bible's benefit comes only when we go on
to believe, accept, and obey it. Only when His Words come to abide in us
(John 15:7) do they lead to Christ and life. Seek Him in His Word and in
prayer, ready to obey. Commune with Him, letting thought, worship, fel-
lowship, and love flow freely back and forth between you and Him.
This Is My Body
Matthew 26:26-28 When Jesus spoke of our eating His flesh and
drinking His blood, He did not mean in the communion supper. He said,
"The flesh profiteth nothing" (John 6:63). The supper is material or flesh-
ly. It cannot give spiritual life or virtue to the partakers. If so, why are we
required to examine ourselves first lest we eat and drink unworthily (1 Co-
rinthians 11:26-27)?
Visible, material forms (the Lord's Supper, baptism, feet washing) are
symbols of spiritual realities. By themselves, they have no value. When
we possess the reality for which it stands, the symbol has sacred meaning.
When we have Christ's life within, we may rightly partake of the symbol
as a testimony to that fact.
What Christ Brings In
When we partake of Christ's flesh and blood, that is, take Him into our
hearts, He brings in all that He is. In Him we have:
LIFE (1 John 5:12): God is the Author of all life. Without Him no life
exists. We can have no spiritual life except by having Jesus Christ within.
Having a religious form, joining a church, being baptized, taking commun-
ion, doing good works, reforming, striving, or good living—none of these
can make the soul live. Christ's entrance does.
DIVINE NATURE (2 Peter 1:4): Through knowing Jesus and His
Father we have all things that pertain unto life and godliness. By believing
and complying with His promises, we have the divine nature—the nature
of God. Jesus promised if we abide in Him and He abides in us, we will
bring "forth much fruit" (John 15:5). This fruit is godliness, holiness, and
spiritual graces that are Christ-like (Galatians 5:22-23). The divine nature
is planted when Christ enters at our repentance and increases as we walk
with Him in obedience each day.
LAWS OF GOD (Hebrews 10:16): The person who is eating, or tak-
ing in, Christ has God's laws written in his being. Thus, doing God's will
is neither dreary drudgery nor an unwilling task. Although it costs hard
work and suffering at times, the motives and desires of the heart accord
with God's laws. The impulse of our hearts will be to do right.
CONSTANT SUPPLY (John 4:14): The living water Jesus brings into
a heart refreshes and gives life to the soul. It becomes a spring ever flow-
ing. It is eternal life begun in this world. It flows into an overflowing
stream, drawing others to the Lord (John 7:37-39).
ALL WE NEED (1 Corinthians 1:30): Christ is made unto us wisdom,
righteousness, sanctification, and redemption. What more do we need?
Colossians 2:9-10 tells us that in Him we have all—a completeness. His
death bought all. If an unbroken connection runs from the power plant to
our house, it brings a flow of electricity to supply light, heat, and power
for any variety of needs. Christ in us is our supply for any need here and
also the perfect life to come. Taste and see that the Lord is good.
JUST A THOUGHT
What is in the well of your heart will show up
in the bucket of your speech.
LESSON 8
EXCEPT A CORN OF WHEAT DIE
Scripture Texts: John 12:23-26; Matthew 10:37-39; Galatians 2:20;
Colossians 3:3; Romans 6:8; 8:13; 12:1; Revelation 12:11
We cannot live the self-life and the Christ-life at the same time. Self-
life must die so that Christ may live in us and that we may be His disci-
ples.
MEMORY VERSE: Verily, verily, I say unto you, Except a corn of wheat
fall into the ground and die, it abideth alone: but if it die, it bringeth forth
much fruit.
—John 12:24
Old Man or New Man
The old man counsels, "Do your best, break off bad habits, work hard,
improve yourself, and be good." Perhaps this is the biggest mistake made
in the religious world—build a good record before man, unite with God,
and you will get to Heaven. What does Jesus say to the old man? Read Ro-
mans 6:6 and Colossians 3:9-10.
Christ's Death and Ours
John 12:23-26 As His death drew very near, Jesus spoke of Himself as
a corn of wheat that must die to bear fruit. Only His death could bring
about the saving of sinners. From Himself, Jesus turned immediately to
speaking of all people. Jesus must die; so must we. Before Jesus died
physically, He died to self. He left Heaven and gave up ease, comfort, and
honor. He hated His life for our sake. For Him, we must hate ours to death
and bury it. This planting will bear fruit of righteousness and union with
Christ.
Matthew 10:37-39 The sacrifice of self to Christ requires us to love
Him above ourselves, relatives, or friends. Bearing the cross is often
thought of as suffering such afflictions and troubles as life brings. But sin-
ners experience these, too, often with courage and patience. When Jesus
took His Cross, He was going to voluntary death. To take up our cross is
to voluntarily die to self and the world. Death is a separation. We must se-
parate from self-interests. Yield our will; lose our life; make Christ all in
all. Without this death we cannot be Jesus' disciples (Luke 14:27).
Death, the Way to Life
Galatians 2:20 Paul identified himself with Christ. He was submerged
in Him, crucified with Christ. He drew life from Him. He ate and drank
of Christ's flesh and blood (Lesson 7). Paul had died; his new life was
Christ. This was a continuing experience as he formed his action by it. He
said, "I die daily" (1 Corinthians 15:31). We must kill the old man and
stand on his grave with a sword every day.
Colossians 3:3 In writing to brethren in Christ, Paul said ye are dead.
Death to sin freed them to be hid with Christ in God. Safely hidden, their
lives joined with Christ's—this is eternal life begun in this world. It is cer-
tainly worth the loss of corrupt, doomed self-life.
Romans 6:8 We accept His sacrificial death as being for us personally.
Joined with Him until His death is our death; His life is our life. This is
baptism into Jesus Christ, as we read in verses 3-6.
Water baptism symbolizes this. The burial in water pictures death to
sinful self—the old man. Rising from the water pictures new life in Christ.
The complete meaning of water baptism includes the filling with the Holy
Spirit (Acts 19:2-6). Jesus' death purchased this for us (Hebrews 10:19).
Complete death to self is rightly pictured only by complete immersion in
water.
Wheat that refuses to die bears no fruit, has no continuing life, no com-
munion with its Maker, no part in His work, no companionship with living
grains, and no growth. What does solitary existence mean to a human
soul? Jesus said that where He is, there would His servant be.
How to Die
Romans 8:13 The wrong kind of life brings death. The right kind of
death brings life (Galatians 6:8). We must put to death the deeds of the
body and repent of them. How can we resist the inclinations of natural,
sinful self? Through the Spirit, by yielding all to Him (Romans 6:13-16).
Only by coupling our decisions and actions with His supernatural power
can we continue to live the Christian life.
Old Testament saints killed and burned animals in sacrifice to God.
God still wants sacrifice from us, but now it is our living bodies that He
desires (Romans 12:1). His saving and cleansing power makes our bodies
holy and acceptable to Him. We yield them to Him to use forever. We are
given details of how they are to be used in the completion of Romans,
Chapter 12.
Revelation 12:11 Saints who loved not their lives unto the death.
Having died to self, they could die for Christ without fear. The victory
was won not when the head dropped lifeless, but when they had laid all on
the altar of Christ—life, possessions, ambitions, loves, will, and all. Satan
is not overcome by half measures. Repent; put faith in Christ; lay all on
His altar. The flame of the Holy Spirit will consume it and live in your
heart.
Counterfeit Death
Down through history, many schools of thought have tried (with varied
success) different methods of conquering self. One is inflicted suffering.
Self is to be killed, not tortured. Beds of spikes do not cleanse away sin
or kill the old man. Another is rigorous abstinence. We are to deny self not
deny TO self. Choosing to abstain from foods we like will not meet the of-
fering for sin.
Another method is repression. The old man is not to be repressed, but
put to death. By determined effort, we can thwart many an evil impulse.
This is not enough. It will only cause self to grow bigger, feeding on the
pride of its own efforts and sacrifices. None of these methods are taking
your cross and following Jesus.
When self is dead, we do not seek recognition or praise. We do not de-
sire to be seen. We are not jealous of praise or favor shown to another. We
do not care who receives credit for what is done, as long as the work is
successful. We forget what we do or suffer and give Christ all the glory.
JUST A THOUGHT
Nothing reveals character
more than self-sacrifice.
LESSON 9
EXCEPT YE BECOME AS LITTLE CHILDREN
Scripture Texts: Matthew 18:2-4; Isaiah 26:4; Luke 11:34; Philippians
4:8; 1 Corinthians 5:8; 14:20; Titus 1:15; James 3:17; 1 Peter 5:5
The first glance at today's lesson title might cause it to appear that
saints are weaklings. But we shall find that to become childlike—trusting
and submissive to our Heavenly Father—does not make us easy prey to
unfair imposition. When children of God submit to God and put their trust
in Him, they find great protection from the wicked schemes of the enemy.
We need never fear what God leads us into. In today's lesson, we learn
what the expression "Be wise as serpents and harmless as doves" means.
MEMORY VERSE: Verily I say unto you, Except ye be converted, and
become as little children, ye shall not enter into the kingdom of heaven.
—Matthew 18:3
Necessity of Childlikeness
Matthew 18:2-4 Except ye be converted, and become as little chil-
dren. We must be changed because we are self-willed, self-dependent, and
stiff-necked. There are many descriptive traits of a child—honest, trust-
ing, dependent, yielding, tender, openhearted, receptive, pure, etc. But
those who know children might say that none quite so adequately defines
the child nature as Jesus' words—as little children. What this nature is,
God wants us to be. The Kingdom of Heaven does not open to the proud,
the self-assertive, or the heart closed by sin. These must be repented of.
We must humble ourselves.
How is a little child humble? Does he protest his unworthiness? Or re-
sent the fact that he is beneath others? He humbly depends on another for
his every need. He is open, frank, and yielding; looking to higher author-
ity, obedient to it. Repentance breeds this childlike attitude in us. Without
it, we cannot be saved (Luke 18:17).
The refreshing change of the newly saved is due to the child nature
springing fresh in their hearts like new growth on a plant. They are hope-
ful, receptive, openly honest, eager, hungry for new light and new duties.
This should continue and does according to how close and obedient we
keep to the Lord.
Some Childlike Qualities We Need
TRUST (Isaiah 26:4): Trust ye in the L ORD , not self. The world ur-
ges us to have faith in ourselves. Faith in ourselves cannot reach far
enough. In the L ORD J EHOVAH is everlasting strength. Trust Him as a
little child trusts his parent. Rest in Him. When a parent puts a child on a
table and tells him to jump, his faith in his parent just naturally causes him
to jump, trusting that his parent will catch him.
SINGLE EYE (Luke 11:34): The straight forward eye, the steady
look, singleness of purpose. A shifting eye casts about for an excuse, a
change, for possible advantage over others. The single eye is settled,
steadfast. It looks to Jesus and deals in truth. Truth is light.
SINCERITY, TRUTH (1 Corinthians 5:8): To have the right to par-
take of the Lord's Supper, your inward spiritual state must be in accor-
dance with the symbolic meaning of the supper. In the heart must be sin-
cerity and truth unmixed with malice and wickedness.
NO MALICE (1 Corinthians 14:20): In malice be ye children—be
ignorant of it. There is a saying, "Children and fools tell the truth." Du-
plicity, hypocrisy, and sly scheming have not yet entered them. They be-
lieve what they hear and speak to be believed.
GOOD THOUGHTS (Philippians 4:8): "As he thinketh in his heart,
so is he" (Proverbs 23:7). Thought is the root of action and character.
Wrong thoughts are as hidden cancer that will break out in corruption and
sin. Pure thoughts blossom into righteousness. Think of the things that are
true, honest, just, pure, lovely, of good report, virtue, and praise. When
evil thrusts itself before us, think pure thoughts to keep free of the guilt.
This is done when we lean upon the Holy Spirit.
PURITY (Titus 1:15): A pure heart sees things in a pure way. As mud
thrown into a spring cannot contaminate it but is quickly washed away, so
is impurity when thrust at a pure heart. "A well of water [that is] springing
up" (John 4:14). It refuses what is contrary to it.
GENTLENESS, EASILY INTREATED (James 3:17): Could this de-
scribe a little child? A saint is easily touched, easy to talk to, and has sym-
pathy for others. The love of God in the heart listens, feels, and is ready
to consider a plea for help. A saint can be inconvenienced and not feel in-
jured.
SUBJECTION, HUMILITY (1 Peter 5:5): All of you be subject.
Saved individuals are not bossy, demanding, proud, or control-seeking.
They are submissive, yielding, cooperative, humble, self-forgetful, and in
honor they prefer one another. For a pattern look at Jesus—the King of
kings. He was "meek and lowly" (Matthew 11:29). He came to minister.
A child nature is planted in the heart with salvation. We must let it
grow. Feed, cultivate, and develop it, refusing temptations to act other-
wise. The Christian life is repression of self and expression of Christ.
Why does Christ esteem singleness of eye and singleness of heart so high-
ly?
Jesus set a little child before us as a sample of that in which He de-
lights. Christ said to become as a little child; the same is greatest in the
Kingdom of Heaven. Should not what is precious to Him be held precious
by us?
He went on to show the dreadful end of those who wrong children. Dis-
cuss some of the ways children are being wronged and led astray in our
land. (Read Matthew 18:6.)
JUST A THOUGHT
"No nation has ever fallen from without until it has
corrupted from within."—C. W. Burpo
LESSON 10
EXCEPT YE HAVE LOVE
Scripture Texts: 1 Corinthians 13:3; Matthew 22:37-40; John 13:34-35;
17:26; 1 John 4:7-8, 18; Galatians 5:6, 14; Romans 5:5; Jude 21
The word love is used very loosely by the world. In this lesson, we will
study together what God calls the highest virtue, the very essence of God
Himself. Is it more than attraction? Or is it care for others? Does it desire
the good of itself or of another? Is it given according as the receiver de-
serves it? Is God's love for us dependent upon what we are or upon what
He is? He is no respecter of persons. He loved us and sent Christ to die
while we were yet sinners. His love working in us will give us love for
even the least lovely. They are the ones who need it most. His love will
not promote love of self but will cause us to love others.
MEMORY VERSE: He that loveth not knoweth not God; for God is love.
—1 John 4:8
Love Is Necessary
1 Corinthians 13:3 The virtue of love is necessary for acceptance with
God. It must be more than natural, human love. It must be the love of God
received through the new birth and Holy Spirit baptism. Paul told us that
no ability, no works, or no virtue can take the place of love. No sacrifice
can make up for lack of love. Love is an absolute essential of salvation, of
spiritual life. Without it we are nothing, lost, and doomed for eternity.
Matthew 22:37-40 To love is the great commandment of God. There-
fore, we cannot please Him without love. All His commands and prom-
ises—the Law and the prophets—depend upon love. They can be accepted
and obeyed as God desires only through love. We are to love God first and
our neighbor second. Our neighbors are our fellow man wherever he may
be found. We cannot love our neighbor rightly until we love God with our
whole heart.
The only way we can love God is with our whole heart, soul, and mind.
Every faculty is to be turned toward exalting Him, is to be spent in adora-
tion of Him. His will must be our first pleasure. Love breeds joyful ser-
vice. What is to measure love for our neighbor? Love for self. Everyone
has a built-in measuring rod of self-love—and the further from God we
are, the greater it grows. Love for self leads to a great number of other sins
(2 Timothy 3:2). When one's self-love is set right, love for others will also
be right.
John 13:34-35 The love binding saints together is the mark by which
the world recognizes the true church. Mere professors cannot pass the love
test.
The Love Test
John 17:26 Has man the capacity to love as commanded? No, unsaved
people do not because they cannot. There is a human love that people have
naturally, but it is limited. Jesus asked His Father to give His people the
love that He gave Him. This marvelous love fills the heart of a saint. The
actual love of God cannot be imitated.
1 John 4:7-8 God is love and love is of God. It takes more than human
love to qualify us as born of God. Jesus said even publicans love those
who love them (Matthew 5:46). We must love with the love of God. Hu-
man love has neither the quality nor the quantity to fill our need. We are
told to love. We try, and we fail, because to love, we must be born of
God, must have Him who is love. "He that dwelleth in love dwelleth in
God" (1 John 4:16). When we have love, we can use that love, but we can-
not manufacture love.
The Working of Love
1 John 4:18 Perfect love casteth out fear. Love comes in when we are
freed from sin and born again, and it increases toward perfection as we
grow in Christ. Peace reigns. Fear is cast out of the heart. Does this mean
nothing can frighten us?
There are two kinds of fear: (1) inward fear that abides, constantly, in
the heart; love casts this fear out; and (2) outward fear caused by a fright-
ening circumstance. This fear will be lessened by the trust in God that
love brings. We may still be frightened by a fierce dog or a violent storm.
Such fear passes.
Galatians 5:6 Outward forms do not increase our spirituality nor gain
favor with God. He looks on the heart. He seeks faith, which worketh by
love. Love nourishes faith, activates it, and opens the way for faith to
work.
Galatians 5:14 All the law is fulfilled in one word—love. How can
we sin in any way against the one we love? When the love of God fills our
heart, it nourishes all other forms of righteousness. Love is composed of
honesty, purity, reverence, faithfulness, etc. The love of God is not given
to certain chosen people only. It was at one time, but now, thank God, it
is for whosoever will. God's love flows out upon all. He causes the rain to
fall on the just and the unjust, alike (Matthew 5:45).
Finding and Keeping Love
Romans 5:5 The love of God is not ours naturally. It must be an opera-
tion of God. We must first repent and put our faith in Christ. Then we are
born of the Spirit. Love comes in. It enters all we do. God teaches us how
to use it (1 Thessalonians 4:9).
Jude 21 Keep yourselves in the love of God. God puts it there, but
there is a part we must do to keep it true within our lives. Obey its im-
pulses; obey the Spirit's leadings. Keep praying, trusting God, studying
and obeying the Bible. "But whoso keepeth his word, in him verily is the
love of God perfected: hereby know we that we are in him" (1 John 2:5).
More Than a Social Gospel
God's requirement of love is not fulfilled in the "social Gospel." This
is the widespread theory that the purpose of the church is to raise the
present condition of people. It seeks their social and economic good. This
is not the goal Christ set. (Read Mark 16:15-16.)
Acts of charity—feeding the hungry, helping the troubled, comforting
the sorrowing—do not fill the whole measure required of Christian love.
The world is easily touched by these needs. They are natural, which is
where the world lives. Worldly people tend to feel this is real Christianity;
this is all there is to it. These acts hold a sure place in a Christian's duty,
but more is required.
The purpose of the church is to supply the spiritual and eternal needs
also. The love of God dictates this right along with the physical or natural
needs. This love brings us glory in the Cross of Christ and in suffering for
His cause.
JUST A THOUGHT
"No man works harder against his own interests than
the man who works for them exclusively."
LESSON 11
EXCEPT YOUR RIGHTEOUSNESS EXCEED
Scripture Texts: Isaiah 28:17; Matthew 5:20; 7:21; Romans 8:1; Philip-
pians 3:8-9; Ephesians 4:11-13, 22-24; 1 John 3:2-9
A doctrine held by those who do not believe in holiness is that all
Christians sin more or less. In our lesson today, we will study what the
Scriptures have to say in regard to this doctrine. How much sin does God
excuse? How much sin do the people of the world excuse?
The world's people have a standard by which they measure professing
Christians. If they see us commit a questionable act, they are usually quick
to doubt our profession. How much sin does God have power to cleanse
from a person's life? What is His promise?
MEMORY VERSE: For I say unto you, That except your righteousness
shall exceed the righteousness of the scribes and Pharisees, ye shall in no
case enter into the kingdom of heaven.
—Matthew 5:20
What God Calls Righteousness
Isaiah 28:17 Perfect righteousness is required. This speaks of God's
sharp eye for judging. He sees clearly, closely, and accurately. We cannot
lie to Him. We cannot hide, for He sees and knows all. He requires per-
fection (Matthew 5:48).
Matthew 5:20 The scribes and Pharisees. The scribes were students
of the Law of Moses and Old Testament Scriptures. They were better at
knowing than obeying them. The Pharisees were strict keepers of the
forms of the Law. They were sticklers for the letter of doctrine. They ad-
ded details (traditions) that were supposed to make observance of forms
more exact. In them, outward form crowded out inward purity.
Both the scribes and Pharisees were self-righteous and hypocritical.
Both had a habit of judging and condemning others. Therefore, Jesus said
our righteousness must be of better quality than theirs. Theirs was out-
ward. Ours must be both outward and inward, spiritual, sincere, complete,
and holy or we will miss the Kingdom of Heaven.
Matthew 7:21 We can say Lord, Lord, from our lips, and it avails
nothing. When it comes from the heart, it means that we obey Jesus as our
Lord. Only those who DO the will of God will enter the Kingdom of Heav-
en.
Romans 8:1 There are some who have no condemnation. They are not
guilty before God. This is a holy position. They reach it by being new
creatures in Jesus Christ. They are led and taught by the Holy Spirit. They
have crucified the flesh (Galatians 5:24; 6:14). This is not done in our own
human power (as the Pharisees obeyed forms). It is by the work of God in
the heart.
Philippians 3:8-9 Paul had been trying to keep the Law and did (verses
4-6). This was his own righteousness, an attainment he earned by his own
efforts. But when he saw God's righteousness and knew that he could have
it (not by working but by grace), he cast away his own righteousness as
nothing to take God's by putting faith in Christ. This was righteousness of
the heart, not of outward works.
By a person's own efforts, he can overcome some bad impulses and
habits, but he cannot change these impulses into holy ones. If he succeeds
in ordering his life after earthly standards of goodness, honesty, kindness,
helpfulness, and generosity, these will never carry him into the Kingdom
of Heaven. They will never serve as the wedding garment at the marriage
of the Lamb. It is only righteousness that God accepts, as the old song of
Zion expresses: "When He shall come with trumpet sound, Oh, may I then
in Him be found; Dressed in His righteousness alone, Faultless to stand
before the throne."
Good works have a place in a Christian's life. "They which have
believed in God might be careful to maintain good works" (Titus 3:8).
Keep doing the works God has generated. If Heaven were to be earned, we
could never do enough good works to earn an eternity of perfect joy. Jesus
purchased the right and power for us to live holy. He purchased it with His
own blood. He paid with His life. What remains for us to pay? The song
is true that says, "Jesus paid it all, All to Him I owe."
Reaching the Standard
Ephesians 4:11-13 Christ has given the church certain leaders or ser-
vants qualified by Him to teach and lead the saints to the state God has set
for them, the state of perfection. This does not mean that we can ever
know all, or that we will never make a mistake. It is not human perfection,
but a perfect heart that God wants, perfect in motive, in purity, in love.
How perfect? Unto the measure of the stature of the fulness of Christ.
No higher standard could be set. The only way we can reach it is to have
Christ within. Paul said in Philippians 4:13, "I can do all things through
Christ which strengtheneth me."
Ephesians 4:22-24 We must put off ... the old man of sin and put on
the new man. This is the spiritual transformation that changes one from
a child of the devil to a child of God. As the inward life is changed, so is
the outward conduct. God's children are trustworthy, honest, true, pure,
kind, helpful, and loving. Their righteousness comes from God. It is His
goodness living in human lives.
1 John 3:2-9 John was speaking of the hope of seeing God's appearing
and seeing him as he is. He brings the plain teaching that we become as
pure and as sinless as Jesus. This is done by being born of God—the only
way to be separated from sin. Man cannot do this in himself. His only part
is to submit to the work of God. When God sees this and does His part, the
man is pure and ceases to sin. He does not sin because the seed of God
lives in his heart. It is holiness. It is the life of God and the direct opposite
of sin. God and sin cannot live in the same place at the same time.
This is the righteousness God requires. He not only requires it, but He
provides it. Our part is to repent, put faith in Christ, and yield ourselves
all to Him through obedience to His Word and the leading of the Holy
Spirit. We provide the vessel; He provides the righteousness. Can there be
any doubt that righteousness is necessary for us to please God?
Present Need
In these perilous times, we hear that "times have changed" and "we
must have new methods, new standards; the old are outdated." This is not
true. Christianity cannot succeed with shifting standards. We do have an
absolute and changeless standard of right and wrong; it does not change
according to circumstances. "If the foundations be destroyed, what can the
righteous do?" (Psalm 11:3). "For ever, O L ORD , thy word is settled in
heaven" (Psalm 119:89). Who set the standard? Where do we find it? Who
will finally judge our measuring to it?
In the midst of rapidly declining moral conditions, blasphemies, mount-
ing crime, drugs, sexual permissiveness, rebellion against authority, ne-
glect of the Bible, failure of the home and of the nominal church, what can
we do? We must hold up before our youth a standard of righteousness that
works.
JUST A THOUGHT
The tragedy of our day is not unanswered prayer
but unoffered prayer.
LESSON 12
EXCEPT YE BE HOLY
Scripture Texts: Ephesians 1:4; 1 Peter 1:15-16; Romans 6:14; 1 John
1:9; Romans 8:1; Titus 2:11-12
In the time of the Law, God commanded the high priest to wear on his
forehead a golden plate bearing the words, HOLINESS TO THE LORD.
Holiness is the offering God desires and requires from His people. His
church is made up of holy people. God does not accept anything short of
holiness. We are either holy or unholy, righteous or unrighteous.
Today we study, very briefly, Bible teachings on holiness. We may find
that holiness is a deeper experience than righteousness, which we studied
in Lesson 11. Most people believe in holiness. The question is, How and
when and where are we made holy?
MEMORY VERSE: Follow peace with all men, and holiness, without
which no man shall see the Lord.
—Hebrews 12:14
The Necessity of Holiness
Ephesians 1:4 Before the foundation of the world. The holiness of
man has been God's plan from the beginning. Man with his nature, abili-
ties, and desires was made to suit a holy life and no other. Unholy living
brings pain, for it does not fit in God's plan.
1 Peter 1:15-16 God's children are born of Him and must be like Him.
Holiness is of such great necessity that "no man shall see the Lord" with-
out it (Hebrews 12:14). Unholiness of the heart damns. This answers the
question "Is holiness necessary?"
Romans 6:14 Sin shall not have dominion over you. When Jesus died
as our sacrifice for sin, He broke sin's dominion over everyone who ac-
cepts His sacrifice. But He did even more than save us from our sins. He
brought in a dispensation of grace in which God's life is put into men to
enable them to do what they never could do in their own power.
The Law commanded righteousness but gave no power to do so. Christ
not only saves us, but through consecration of ourselves and setting our-
selves apart for His holy use, we are given power to live holy every day.
The Possibility of Holiness
Some people differ with teachers of holiness because they are really
opposed to the doctrine. Ask them, "If it were possible to live holy, would
you desire to?" Note the answer that you receive. Others differ because of
misunderstanding of terms. Holiness is sinlessness, we say. Yes, but it is
more. Negatively, it is sinlessness, or the absence of sin. Positively, it is
the presence of godliness—of the nature of God. God is holy. Holiness is
God-likeness.
God's nature in a man makes his character holy. The saint has the
power of God at his disposal to enable him to have victory over sin. If we
are continually conscious of this fact, we will continually depend upon
God for victory over trials and temptations, which Satan is sure to send.
1 John 1:9 God meets the repentant sinner with forgiveness and cleans-
ing from all that is contrary to God. When that is done, the man is holy.
Romans 8:1 There is a people who are not condemned—no blame, no
guilt, no accusation from God. They live holy lives because they are in
Christ Jesus. They are still on earth just as other people—eating, sleeping,
and working as usual. But they walk not after ... that is, they do not fol-
low the lust of ... the flesh. The best argument for holiness is a holy life.
God requires holiness, but He provides all we need to obtain it.
The Meaning of Holiness
Titus 2:11-12 Holiness is simply being godly right here in this present
world. Not in some future time, but now. Holiness is not freedom from
mistakes. We all make mistakes. A godly person corrects them when pos-
sible. An oft heard remark is, "No one is perfect." No, not perfect from
mistakes, but perfect regarding sin. "Be ye therefore perfect, even as your
Father which is in heaven is perfect" (Matthew 5:48). Some may believe
that sinless living is impossible because of misunderstanding the differ-
ence between sin and mistakes.
Mistakes may bring undesirable results but never guilt. Examples: giv-
ing wrong information while thinking it is true; having an auto accident;
etc. These are mistakes not sins. Sins are done from wrong motives, know-
ing it is wrong with a disregard for God's will.
Holiness is not the impossibility of sinning. Anyone can turn from God
and sin if he chooses. Holiness is the ability to keep from sinning, made
possible by the power of God within. Our hearts can be perfectly clean,
our motives perfectly pure, and the love of our hearts perfectly set upon
God.
What we do may not be much, but it must be pure all through to meet
God's approval. We are all weak and make many mistakes. That is why
God has not left the issue depending upon our own strength, but upon HIS.
JUST A THOUGHT
The fellow who is pulling the oars does not have
any time to rock the boat.
LESSON 13
EXCEPT YE HOLD STEADFAST
Scripture Texts: 1 Peter 5:8-10; Matthew 24:9-13; Hebrews 3:14; James
In our lesson today, we will learn that God will have a tried people,
tested and proven qualified for His purposes. He does not promise to spare
us from suffering or persecution (2 Timothy 3:12). He will send a shaking
time. We will find that it is possible for a person once saved to be lost af-
terward and go to hell. The man not fit for the kingdom had put his hand
to the plow, but looked back (Luke 9:62). Jesus said, "The love of many
shall wax cold" (Matthew 24:12). We find that there are many conditional
promises in our lesson Scriptures.
There is courage and strength to be gained from knowing of others'
sufferings and persecutions, and of their successes or failures.
MEMORY VERSE: For we are made partakers of Christ, if we hold the be-
ginning of our confidence stedfast unto the end.
—Hebrews 3:14
The Battle
1 Peter 5:8-10 The moment we are saved, we place ourselves upon the
battlefield for Christ. We declare war on Satan and his forces. The devil
and his servants are set for the turning back of EVERY child of God. He
walketh about. He is working to deceive and trip us unexpectedly. In this
world, we are never free from the liability of temptation. If we yield, we
are lost.
There is but one defense in this spiritual battle—God. We are to resist,
to be sober, be vigilant, ever watchful. We must always beware of trust-
ing in our own strength (1 Corinthians 10:12). Resistance must be in the
faith, in the God of all grace. We must take our stand and make a start,
then God will come with His strength. Keep steadfast, trust in Him, and
He will make you perfect, stablish, strengthen, settle you. This is God's
way to bring you out of the temptation stronger in Christ than before.
Matthew 24:9-13 Can anyone doubt that the Christian life is a battle?
Some shall survive true to Christ, but many will be offended, turned
aside, shall betray ... and shall hate one another. The love of many
shall wax cold. Many will be deceived by false teachings.
Many false prophets shall arise. Do we have any now? These are not
honest Christian brethren who see some points of belief differently than
other brothers do. These are deliberate opposers of Jesus Christ. To follow
them is to be deceived, or led into darkness. Such are any disbelievers in
Christ and the Bible, posing as Christian ministers who teach doctrines
that will keep us from life in Christ. God's Word tells us how we can keep
ourselves free and help protect others from deceptive teachings (Matthew
Hebrews 3:14 Stedfast unto the end. The battle is not reserved for
some future time, it is happening now. The enemy's purpose is to stamp
out Christianity through opposition, hardship, suffering, prison, torture,
and death. To be made partakers of Christ, we must hold ... stedfast un-
to the end. The battle is spiritual. Thus, carnal weapons will not gain us
victory. The devil has many methods of turning us from Christ. One is the
cares of this world and the deceitfulness of riches (Matthew 13:22).
James 1:12 He shall receive the crown of life. Crowns imply victory,
honor, power, and authority. This is an incorruptible crown (1 Corinthians
9:25). It is for those who endure faithfully. It is eternal life in Christ Jesus.
Strength to Overcome
2 Timothy 1:13-14 These verses outline requirements for holding true
to Christ. Two instructions cover it. (1) Hold fast the form of sound
words. We must study, heed, love, and obey God's Word. The way we
obey is through faith and love, which are by Christ Jesus. Not our own
failing human striving, but by that faith and love that Jesus brings into our
hearts. (2) That good thing ... keep by the Holy Ghost. The good thing
is the life received from God when He saved us.
The Holy Spirit will guide us to keep our union with God strong. He is
the greatest safeguard we have. Obey Him. "Not to the strong is the battle,
Not to the swift is the race, Yet to the true and the faithful Vict'ry is prom-
ised through grace."
JUST A THOUGHT
It's a lot more fun to stop adding up your troubles,
and turn to counting your blessings.
